findings.finding: Dancing helps improve balance, coordination, posture, and muscle strength across various ages.
findings.quote: Dance also increases core strength which can improve balance, coordination, and posture (which can, in turn, reduce mechanical back pain).

findings.finding: Structured dance interventions significantly improve body composition, blood biomarkers, and musculoskeletal function.
findings.quote: Meta-analyses showed dance interventions significantly improved body composition, blood biomarkers, and musculoskeletal function.

findings.finding: Long-term dancing interventions can improve balance abilities and hippocampal brain structures in older adults.
findings.quote: Moreover, only the dancers achieved a significant increase in the balance composite score.

findings.finding: Proper warmups, technique, and avoiding dancing through pain help prevent common injuries in training.
findings.quote: Warming up and cooling down exercises are recommended before and after exercises to avoid strain, muscle pains, and possible injury.

principle: Structured dance practice across the lifespan significantly improves physical health, balance, and cognitive function while requiring careful attention to injury prevention.
for_the_teacher: Always lead the learners through a proper warm-up before starting movements to prevent injury.
Remind learners not to push through pain and to stop and rest when needed.
